short.lead: You said 'Shout spells, rob castles, feed the Ophan' is close, but a stranger does not know what the Ophan is. These four keep the first two beats and hint at the Ophan instead of naming it, using your own summary of the loop: plunder, cast, escape, sell, upgrade, meet its demands until you can defeat it.

Last beat
Hinting at the Ophan
you
Your loop: plunder, cast spells, escape alive, sell, upgrade, and meet the Ophan's demands until you can grow strong enough to defeat it.
Like Lethal Company, but the quota is a specific artifact, progression persists, and there is a long goal shared with friends.
Each option names what the Ophan is to you (it owns you, it wants things, you will beat it) rather than what it is called.
Pick one, or write your own.

choices: Which last beat hints at the Ophan best?
"Shout spells, rob castles, feed the thing that owns you."
Servitude and mystery in one phrase; a viewer wants to see 'the thing'.
"Shout spells, rob castles, pay your master, until you can kill it."
Says the long goal outright: serve now, kill it later.
"Shout spells, rob castles, feed the monster that hunts you."
Adds the fear of being hunted, which the last 60 seconds of a raid deliver.
"Shout spells, rob castles, serve it, then slay it."
The shortest; 'it' stays a mystery, and the arc is in four words.
It keeps the rhythm of the line you liked and makes a stranger ask what owns them, which is the hook.
